material_findings: On the normal/default public path, archive members are selected on adaptive search/dev scores and held-out tests are run only after search for adapters that own a genuine test split; final test does not choose archive members or continue evolution.
Archive-best held-out score is a dev/search-selected per-task portfolio evaluated on held-out data, distinct from one best single lineage and distinct from a test-outcome oracle.

Public split types differ materially: CO-Bench and text classification are held_out; ARC-AGI-2 is proxy; OpenEvolve family is dev_equals_test; terminal-bench and SWE-bench expose no separate test adapter through this orchestrator.

The paper itself preserves several of these distinctions: held-out tables for CO/S2D/LawBench, direct benchmark score for AE Math/AlgoTune/SR, and ARC table dev score with held-out result reported separately.
ARC source explicitly warns that split-aware overfit protection is not wired into archive selection, although its final test remains separate on the normal path.
CO-Bench search uses get_dev instance indices while final test uses the disjoint non-dev complement; ordinary TaskDescription metadata does not contain those held-out instances.

Text-classification search uses val while final test uses a separate test split; val per-case payload is deliberately excluded from metadata visible to Omega, while label vocabulary and train few-shot examples are visible.

Important correction: with explicit --verified-code on a crew-scheduling-only CO run, a sandboxed verifier consults the held-out TEST split during candidate construction. The flag is default OFF, bundled benchmark features do not enable it, and source comments call it forensic/build-only/unmeasured. A run using it cannot call the same CO test an untouched outer test.

The persistence layer is locally replay-capable (candidate parent graph, traces, injected code, raw Omega prompt/response, RNG/checkpoint state, LLM I/O), but experiment outputs are ignored and the paper-run stochastic proposal chronology is not published in the inspected Git tree.
blockers: Exact pre-public executable/config and paper-run experiment archives are not publicly source-bound in the inspected Meta^n Git history.
The exact non-deterministic proposal chronology behind reported paper runs is not available in the inspected repository, preventing matched acceptor/archive replay.
